newsitem.title: USA: Caribbean Cigar Q1 loss widens, sales grow.
newsitem.headline: Caribbean Cigar Q1 loss widens, sales grow.

text.p: Caribbean Cigar Co said its net loss for the first fiscal quarter ending June 30, 1996 grew to $276,983, compared to $25,754 for the same period last year.
The company, which went public in early August, said the net loss is due to building an infrastructure, marketing costs associated with creating three national cigar brands, and other expenses.
It said first quarter sales grew to $1,272,307, up 967 percent from the year-ago period sales of $119,200.
Gross profit grew to $386,600, or 30 percent of sales for the three months ended June 30, 1996 compared to $24,800, or 21 percent of sales in the three months ended June 30, 1995.

Caribbean Cigar Company President Kevin Doyle said in a statement, "The cigar industry is in a period of explosive growth. This is especially true in terms of premium cigars. We are positioning the company to take full advantage of this exceptional opportunity."
